component.name: ZAtlas
component.summary: A map of a codebase you have never seen before

description.p: Point ZAtlas at a repository and it draws the actual shape of it: the module dependency graph, every import cycle, a treemap of where the mass is, which files change together, which files change constantly, what is dead and what has become a god-object.

It reads TypeScript, JavaScript, Rust, Python and Go, and reads your git history for churn, ownership and co-change coupling. Findings are ranked and explainable: each one carries the evidence behind it, why it is a finding, and what to do about it.
An import it cannot resolve is recorded with a reason and shown to you rather than quietly dropped, because a dependency graph that is silently wrong is worse than no graph at all.
Four ways to look at the same graph:

ul.li: Graph — the dependency network, laid out deterministically
Treemap — where the lines of code actually are
Matrix — the dependency structure matrix, for spotting tangles
Timeline — the codebase over the last year, scrubbable and playable

description.p: Entirely local and entirely offline. There is no account, no telemetry and no network call. It never modifies your source or your history: git is read straight from the object database and nothing is ever checked out.
